title: Equidistribution of Primitive Sextic Torus Packets
main_claim: Take totally real sextic fields K_i that have no proper intermediate field and whose discriminants go to infinity. Their complete ideal-class packets of compact A-orbits in SL_6(Z)\SL_6(R) become equidistributed to Haar measure, with no escape of mass. The packets include all sign translates, are weighted by orbit volume, and the result holds for any ordering of the real embeddings.

issues.description: The bound kappa >> 1/log D, and through it the Shiu interval bound carrying the kappa factor, rests on Stark's Lemma 8 for fields that are not normal: a real zero in [1-1/(4*6! log D),1) must come from a quadratic subfield. The paper paraphrases this and does not check the hypotheses against the original. I believe the paraphrase is correct (the n! comes from the degree of the Galois closure), but I did not verify it against Stark 1974. Everything else in the zero-exclusion and log-derivative estimate checks out, including the termwise comparison of sum Re 1/(s-rho) on (1, 1+1/log D].
issues.evidence: "His Lemma~8 applies also to nonnormal fields: a real zero beta with 1-1/(4*6! log D) <= beta < 1 would be a zero of the zeta function of a quadratic subfield of K"

issues.description: The ELMV entropy criterion (ELMV2009 Cor. 3.3) is used 'in the form needed here': a two-sided tube bound C e^{-2 eta t_i} implies h >= eta, with the neighborhood allowed to depend on Omega and the space noncompact. This matches my understanding of the criterion, but the paper restates it rather than quoting it, and I did not check it against the source.
issues.evidence: "In the form needed here, it says that if probabilities nu_i invariant under a(R b) converge to a probability nu ... implies h_nu(T) >= eta."

coverage:
I read the whole LaTeX source: introduction, arithmetic, homogeneous, conditioning, product, activity, entropy, combination and assembly. Checked by hand:
(1) Arithmetic: the orbit volume (s/2)R_K, the orbit count 2^6 h/s, and the identity Q kappa = 32 h R (consistent with the class-number formula, r1=6, w=2). The Stark/Hadamard log-derivative argument giving zeta_K(1+1/log D) ≍ kappa log D. The Shiu/Pollack interval bound with exponent bookkeeping (y >= x^{1/2}, x in [D^{1/4}, D]). Both cusp-bound regimes. The r^6 ordinary-ball bound. In the trace-slice lemma: the codifferent covolume 1/Q, the trace-plane spacing 1/sqrt6, the 30th-power discriminant bound, and transference. In the tube estimate: crossing entries O(e^{-t}), the commutator [h,P_S], the dual-lattice computation, the pair-product z in the codifferent, the divisor bound exp(C log D/loglog D) = o(T_-), and D^{-1/30} = o(e^{-T_+}).
(2) Homogeneous: the unimodularity/degree-balance argument forcing block groups; the rational-commutant argument showing the commutant algebra is a field, giving equal block sizes and a central unit fixing the orbit; the fixed-point pieces meeting crossing plaques in at most one point.
(3) Conditioning and product: the martingale plateau selection; patch comparison; the projective plaque comparison, including long wall motions with scale order l_- < R < F < l_+; the U-factor via contraction; the W-factor via tile information cost C sqrt(j(1+S)/T); the Heisenberg transitivity argument.
(4) Activity, entropy and combination: the atom-plus-dilation argument for inactivity on countable sections; the lower bound on name entropy from tubes at the midpoint time N/2 in [T_-,T_+]; the upper bound via transverse-label cost, z-concentration under inactivity, and the e^{C delta M} slow-direction mesh; root-line functions, strong connectivity from cut activity, the two-root cycle with mean-zero densities, and the uniform local CLT convolution bound.
I did not verify the cited external theorems (EKL 2006 Thm 1.3, ELMV Cor 3.3, Stark Lemmas 3 and 8, Pollack Thm 1.1) against their sources. I did not run any numerical checks. The measure-theoretic bookkeeping in the conditioning sections was checked at the level of scale orderings and error terms, not line by line.
